The Laffer Curve is the economic principle that as tax rates rise, tax revenues will eventually hit a tipping point where tax revenues fall due to people working less. E.g. if tax rates were 95%, most people would stop working more than the bare minimum since leisure would be far more valuable to them.

I propose that tax havens are a real world example of the Laffer Curve at a macro level. Instead of working less, corporations incorporate less in high tax areas as taxes rise, eventually causing tax revenues to fall in response to tax rate hikes.

Which begs the question: why do governments ignore this macro-level Laffer Curve and fail to lower corporate tax rates below the tipping point where the incorporation hokey-pokey becomes worthwhile? Are they bad at economics, or just trying to subsidize tax havens like the island of Jersey?
